headword: {石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん}
reading: いしのうえにもさんねん

definitions.gloss: perseverance pays off, patience brings success
definitions.explanation: Literally 'even sitting on a stone for three years' - persistence and patience will eventually bring results.

examples.japanese: 「{石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん}」というから、もう{少|すこ}し{頑張|がんば}ろう。
examples.english: As the saying goes 'perseverance pays off,' so let's keep trying a bit longer.

examples.japanese: {石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん}で、やっと{仕事|しごと}に{慣|な}れた。
examples.english: After three years of persistence, I finally got used to the job.

examples.japanese: {石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん}の{気持|きも}ちで{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: I'm continuing with the mindset of 'perseverance pays off.'

notes:
LITERAL MEANING: "Even on a stone, three years" - referring to how even a cold stone will become warm if you sit on it for three years.

USAGE: Used to encourage persistence and patience, especially in difficult situations or when learning new skills.

NUANCE: Often cited when advising someone to stick with something (a job, study, relationship) rather than giving up too quickly.

SIMILAR PROVERBS:
・{継続|けいぞく}は{力|ちから}なり - Continuity is power
・{七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}き - Fall seven times, get up eight

ENGLISH EQUIVALENTS:
・"Rome wasn't built in a day"
・"Patience is a virtue"
・"Good things come to those who wait"
